note: The TypeScript lane's own recorded slices of the nflverse releases (research-ts/src/projections/nflverse/fixtures, recorded 2026-08-27, byte for byte), used as the EARLIER release a case lands first so today's recording lands on top of it. Real slices of real nflverse release assets, byte-for-byte as published, narrowed to Buffalo's weeks 1-3 of the 2024 regular season so the whole corpus stays a few tens of kilobytes. One team over three weeks is deliberate: it carries a full offensive-snap denominator (a lineman at 100% of snaps), a quarterback, backs and receivers with real target shares, players who appear in one file and not the other, and enough weeks for a rolling window and a backtest replay to have something to walk. Every column the upstream release publishes is kept, including the ones no mapper reads yet, so a schema change upstream is visible here as a diff rather than as a silent drop.

responses.filtered: every person the other two slices reference by pfr_id or gsis_id, plus five players who retired after 2023 (Latavius Murray, Matt Breida, DeVante Parker, Jerick McKinnon, Logan Thomas) and the retired centre who shares Josh Allen's name. The retirees are the point: Phase 1 measured them as the reason a roster-snapshot join loses ten points of resolution per season going back, and the two Josh Allens are the case a name join cannot settle and an id join never has to. One pfr_id in the snap-counts slice (AndeAl01) is genuinely absent from the release, which keeps a real unresolved case in the corpus.

season=2024, week=1, team=BUF. Week one only, because week one is the only weekly roster whose knowable-before-the-opener claim is true (the league's cutdown to fifty-three is a deadline in late August) and the only one `preseason_rosters` stores. The slice keeps every status the release emits for one club, so the coarsening in `rosterStatusOf` has an active list, a reserve list, a practice squad and a cut list to be tested against rather than only the happy path.

season=2020, position in QB/RB/WR/TE. One whole skill-position draft class (78 picks, rounds 1-7) rather than a handful of hand-picked rows, because the curve fit reads pick-to-pick spacing and a thin hand-written table would test our understanding of the shape rather than the shape itself. Keeps two real Cole McDonald rows (round 7, pick 224, blank gsis_id) exactly as the release publishes them — a round-seven quarterback pfr never assigned an NFL id — which is the real case `mapDraftPicks` drops rather than a synthetic one.

season=2024, game_type=REG, week in 1..3, team=BUF. Real rows, byte-for-byte: a player listed with practice information but no game-status designation yet (Cole Bishop, week 1 — the empty `report_status` the archive stores verbatim rather than coalescing to a guess), the full Out/Doubtful/Questionable spread (Javon Solomon's oblique moves Out -> Doubtful -> healthy across the three weeks), and Josh Allen himself carrying a practice-only hand note in weeks 2-3 while never missing a game — the ordinary case of being on the report at all without it costing him a start.

season=2025, game_type=REG, week in 1..3, team=BUF. THE POST-2025 SCHEMA, captured byte-for-byte: `season_type` is now a published column and `date_modified` is gone entirely — nflverse stopped stamping a filing timestamp on this release starting with the 2025 season. Real rows: Tre'Davious White moving Doubtful -> Questionable week 1 to week 2, and several players (Elijah Moore, Khalil Shakir, Dawson Knox among them) carrying practice-only notes with a blank `report_status`, exactly as the 2013-2024 shape does — the only thing that changed is the columns, never the values.

season=2025, game_type=REG, week in {1, 4, 5, 18}, team=NYG. THE REAL SEASON-ENDING-IR CASE THIS MODULE WAS BUILT TO CLOSE: Malik Nabers (gsis_id 00-0039337) reads `status=ACT` in weeks 1 and 4 and `status=RES` in weeks 5 and 18 — the real, measured shape of an ACL tear that ended his 2025 season with him vanishing from the weekly injury report but never from the roster. Four non-consecutive weeks (rather than a contiguous run) keep the slice small while still spanning the whole season: week 1 (active baseline), week 4 (his real last active week), week 5 (the first reserve week, the derivation's anchor), and week 18 (season's end, confirming the placement held). Every other NYG player on those four rosters is kept too, giving the full `status` spread a real file emits (ACT/RES/DEV/CUT/RET/INA and friends) rather than one hand-picked row.
